skills.title: Find low-leverage workflows
skills.summary: Break repeated work into steps and choose one small AI experiment. Keep useful learning and ownership visible.
skills.toolingSummary: Works with supplied examples. Slack or Teams, issue trackers, repositories and document connectors are optional when the chosen context needs them.
skills.executionScope: Identify opportunities and propose a reviewed experiment; installing or reading the skill does not grant tool access or authorize external changes.
skills.requestAction: help me apply the AI Leverage Framework
skills.requestContext:
Recurring task: [what happens and how often]
Current steps: [how you do it today]
People: [who does it and who owns the outcome]
Keep human: [judgment, relationships or learning to protect]
Time and example: [if available]

Start with my recent work. Identify repeated steps I could improve, what judgment or learning to protect and one small experiment to try. Work from the examples I provide or read access I authorize. Propose what to make room for and how to assess whether the experiment helped.

firstUse.result: One repeated task to improve, with a small AI experiment to try.
context: One recurring task and its current steps.
Who does the work and who owns the outcome.
Human judgment or useful practice to protect.
Time spent and a recent example, if available.
checks: Protect the person’s ownership and learning.
Agree on success checks and a stopping point.

skills.title: Daily debrief and follow-through
skills.summary: Turn scattered notes and messages into an action list that checks earlier commitments and links back to evidence.
skills.toolingSummary: Start with approved excerpts. For connected use, choose only the email, chat, documents, comments or delivery records relevant to your focus.
skills.executionScope: Prepare a private reviewable brief. Reading the skill does not authorize sending follow-ups, changing tasks or creating a recurring schedule.
skills.requestContext: Me: [name or handle]. Work focus: [leader, individual contributor or mixed]. Ask if my identity, focus, timezone, day or source scope is unclear. Use supplied material or scoped read access I authorize. A previous brief is optional. Compare commitments with observed evidence and return a private Tonight, Tomorrow and Tracking draft. Keep uncertainty visible. Do not send messages, change tasks or create a schedule.

firstUse.result: A sourced action list for Tonight, Tomorrow and Tracking.
context: Your name, the day and your timezone.
Calendar entries, meeting notes and messages from that day.
Your previous debrief, if you have one.
checks: Choose your priorities; the agent sends nothing.

skills.title: Review feedback and propose improvements
skills.summary: Turn recurring feedback into a proposed correction, with evidence and a way to check it.
skills.toolingSummary: Use selected feedback, current guidance and criteria. Slack or Teams, document or repository read tools are optional; a replay runner is needed only to claim an executed comparison.
skills.executionScope: Return a reviewable proposal and actual comparisons or an unrun plan. Publishing, messaging and scheduling require separate authorization.
skills.requestAction: review selected feedback and propose an improvement
skills.requestContext:
Feedback: [dated excerpts and source labels]
Current guidance: [the content or answer to check]
Criteria: [what a good result must satisfy]
Focus: [one issue to investigate]

Use the feedback, sources and criteria I provide, or scoped read access I authorize. Keep observations separate from AI assessments. Return the finding, a proposed correction and the evidence a person needs to decide. Do not publish the change.

firstUse.result: A proposed fix, with the feedback and evidence behind it.
context: Feedback or support threads with dates and source labels.
The current answer, content or guidance.
Criteria for judging it and one change to investigate.
checks: Verify the finding against the source.
Approve, revise or reject the proposed change.

skills.title: Build reusable context
skills.summary: Put answers, sources and open questions in one starting point the next person or agent can reuse.
skills.toolingSummary: Use approved documents, code and conversations or supplied excerpts. Repository, document and Slack or Teams read tools are optional when the context needs them.
skills.executionScope: Prepare a draft with sources and gaps. Reading this skill does not authorize publishing documentation or changing shared sources.
skills.requestAction: build a reusable knowledge starting point
skills.requestContext:
Reader: [who needs this]
Questions: [what they need to understand]
Sources: [approved excerpts with dates and references]
Scope: [what to include or leave out]

Ask which questions the next reader needs to answer. Use the material I provide or scoped read access I authorize. Return referenced explanations, an entry point and gaps to review. Keep uncertain claims visible and return a draft.

firstUse.result: A referenced guide for the next reader, with an entry point and unanswered questions.
context: The questions the next reader needs to answer.
Relevant documents, code or conversations with source labels.
The intended reader and any scope limits.
checks: Check important claims and conflicting sources.
Resolve gaps before publishing shared guidance.

skills.title: Delegate work you can review
skills.summary: Turn a vague handoff into a task brief or reviewable result, with boundaries, acceptance checks and a stopping point.
skills.toolingSummary: Supplied context is enough for a brief. Implementation needs an authorized working area and relevant checks; remote repository or document access is optional.
skills.executionScope: Follow the actual request for planning or execution. A skill is not permission to write, create a remote review, merge, deploy or run without a stopping point.
skills.requestAction: prepare or carry out work I can review
skills.requestContext:
Goal: [the outcome]
Current material: [approved context or working area]
Boundaries: [allowed changes and constraints]
Acceptance: [how to check the result]
Stop after: [brief, draft or another explicit stopping point]

Start from my goal and establish the scope, constraints, acceptance checks and stopping point. If I request a brief, return the brief. If I request execution, use only the working area and actions I authorize. Return an inspectable result and actual checks.

firstUse.result: A task brief or reviewable result, with clear checks and a stopping point.
context: The outcome you want and the current material.
What may change and what must stay unchanged.
Acceptance checks and where the agent should stop.
checks: Confirm the scope and acceptance checks.
Review evidence before accepting any completed work.

skills.title: Check whether the automation is helping
skills.summary: Compare preparation, review, corrections and upkeep before deciding whether to keep an automation.
skills.toolingSummary: Works with supplied measurements. Reporting, issue, timing-log or file read tools are optional; no live connector is required.
skills.executionScope: Assess the evidence and propose the next measurement. This skill does not change workflows, assign people or create tracking.
skills.requestAction: assess whether one workflow is helping
skills.requestContext:
Task and period: [what you compared]
Cases: [comparable completed work, including failures]
Human effort: [preparation, review, corrections and upkeep]
Quality and setup: [measured results and costs]
Unknowns: [anything not measured]

Use comparable cases and the measurements I provide. Include human preparation, review, correction and maintenance. Keep unknowns and setup costs visible. Separate effort from quality, cost and what the attention enabled. Return a decision draft and one next measurement.
skills.talkTitle: Check whether the automation is helping

firstUse.result: An effort comparison and a keep, revise or stop recommendation.
context: The task, time period and comparable completed cases.
Human preparation, review, correction and maintenance time.
Quality checks, setup costs and anything not measured.
checks: Keep unknowns visible; you decide whether to keep, revise or stop the automation.
